thread.title: Midday Update: Stocks Lose Ground as Higher Yields And Tech Sector Selling Weighs on Wall Street

title: Midday Update: Stocks Lose Ground as Higher Yields And Tech Sector Selling Weighs on Wall Street
text:
Midday Update: Stocks Lose Ground as Higher Yields And Tech Sector Selling Weighs on Wall Street April 20, 2018, 01:00:40 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo 
Wall Street's major averages were beaten down for a second day Friday as higher Treasury yields and pressure on the technology sector overshadowed strong quarterly results from Dow component stock General Electric ( GE ) and strength in the banking sector. 
The fallout from soft revenue guidance from Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) and a warning about sluggish demand for smartphones weighed on Apple ( AAPL ), causing the iPhone maker to contribute as much as 40 points to the 200+ point slide in the blue chip index. 
Selling pressure on the semiconductor sector was amplified by the backlash in China following the US ban on sales to ZTE Corp, China's second largest telecom equipment maker. The outcry against the US rekindled trade war jitters and sent shares of US chipmakers sharply lower. 
Commodities were mostly lower as gold, hurt by the stronger dollar, continued to lose ground despite greater risk aversion, while oil was weighed down by President Trump's tweet about OPEC being behind the "artificially high" prices. 
On the plus side, corporate earnings were mostly bullish with GE, Honeywell ( HON ), Ericsson ( ERIC ) and Schlumberger (SLB) beating Wall Street's expectations. Skechers (SKX) beat Q1 forecasts, but a downbeat outlook for Q2 caused the stock price to fall by as much as 30% to its lowest level since October (pre-stock split). 
Buoyed by dovish comments from European Central Bank President Mario Draghi and the corresponding impact on the euro, the Euro-Stoxx market index closed fractionally higher, overcoming sizable losses in US equities. In a statement at the International Monetary and Finance Committee (IMFC), Draghi said ample monetary accommodation was still needed and the Eurozone growth cycle may have peaked, fueling speculation that the ECB will maintain its expansive monetary policy. 
Crude oil was down $0.05 to $68.24 per barrel. Natural gas was up $0.06 to $2.72 per 1 million BTU. Gold was down $8.40 to $1,340.40 an ounce, while silver was down $0.04 to $17.19 an ounce. Copper was up $0.003 to $3.13 per pound. 
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 0.14% to $13.79 with the United States Natural Gas Fund was up 1.45% to $22.41. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was down 1.35% to 22.76 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 0.56% to $126.89. The iShares Silver Trust was down 0.38% to $16.19.
